ety.text: Ancient Greek ᾰ̓νᾰρχῐ́ᾱ (ănărkhĭ́ā)der. New Latin anarchiader. English anarchy From New Latin anarchia, from Ancient Greek ἀναρχία (anarkhía). By surface analysis, an- + -archy.

senses.d: The state of a society being without authorities or an authoritative governing body.
ex: Oui, l’anarchie c’est l'ordre; car, le gouvernement c’est la guerre civile.

senses.d: The political theory that a community is best organized by the voluntary cooperation of individuals, rather than by a government, which is regarded as being coercive by nature.
A chaotic and confusing absence of any form of political authority or government.
ex:
And each dweller, panic-stricken,
Felt his heart with terror sicken
Hearing the tempestuous cry
Of the triumph of Anarchy.

senses.d: Confusion in general; disorder.
ex: It was total anarchy in the clothes shop on Black Friday as soon as they opened the doors.
The economic anarchy of capitalist society as it exists today is, in my opinion, the real source of the evil.

grp.label: absence of any form of political authority or government

fr:anarchie.gl: anarchy, absence of any form of political authority or government

senses.d: A structural derivative of a parent compound that differs from it by only one or a few atoms or substituent groups; (usually, especially) such a molecule that retains most of the same chemical properties.
